battle.name: 邠州之戰
battle.brief: 廣德二年（764）八月，叛將僕固懷恩引吐蕃、回紥十萬眾，自靈武、奉天兩路直取邠州；守將白孝德與郭晞閉城拒戰，郭子儀率援軍夜襲敵營於乾陵南，聯軍敗走涇水，邠州之圍解。卡面所繪的亞述長矛未現於此戰，但兩軍步騎所用的長柄矛與短刃，正是同一類冷兵器技術的遠裔。

kit.name: 亞述長矛
kit.history: 短柄、長刃，配著鐵鏃。亞述人把它和弓、鐵器綁在一起，兩河流域的城一個接一個陷落。

countries: 唐軍方面以朔方軍為主體，由時任檢校太尉、中書令、汾陽郡王郭子儀總攬節制，屯兵涇陽，節制河東、關中各鎮兵馬。邠州城由邠寧節度使白孝德據守，閉城自守，不與敵接戰；郭子儀第三子、朔方兵馬使郭晞領一萬人往援邠州，右兵馬使李國臣為其後援。京師宿衛、禁軍及沿邊諸鎮調集之兵亦受郭子儀節制，唐廷另遣中使隨軍監軍，以朝廷詔書為行事之憑。敵方是吐蕃與回紥聯軍：吐蕃自河西、河隴出動，回紥騎兵自漠北南下，合兵號稱十萬眾，並擁立金城公主之兄廣武王李承宏為帝，名義上作為唐室傀儡，實則自領。聯軍之中還夾雜唐朝叛將、河北副元帥僕固懷恩所領的私兵與朔方舊部數萬眾，僕固懷恩是全軍名號所歸，實際指揮權卻仍在吐蕃、回紥諸將手中。唐廷一方是名分上的正統，實際上依靠郭子儀的宿將威望，以及關中殘存的兵馬、糧秣與城防撐住局面。
countriesEn: The Tang side was built around the Northern Frontier Army (Shuofang) and was placed under the overall command of Guo Ziyi, then holding the titles of Grand Commander of the Imperial Guards, Minister of the Secretariat and Prince of Fenyang, who camped at Jingyang and directed the troops of Hedong and the Guanzhong garrisons. The city of Binzhou itself was held by Bai Xiaode, Military Governor of Binning, who shut the gates and refused to give battle; Guo Xi, the third son of Guo Ziyi and Commander of the Shuofang cavalry and infantry, took ten thousand men to relieve the city, with Li Guochen, Commander of the Right Division, serving as his rear support. The imperial guards, the palace garrison and the contingents summoned from the frontier commands were likewise under Guo Ziyi's orders, and the court additionally sent eunuch commissioners to watch the army, so that everything was done on the strength of imperial decrees. The enemy was a combined Tibetan and Uyghur host: the Tibetans moved out of Hexi and the Long region, the Uyghur cavalry came south from the northern steppe, and the two were said to number one hundred thousand men in all, while they set up Li Chenghong, elder brother of the Tang princess Jincheng and known as the Prince of Guangwu, as emperor, a puppet of the Tang house in name only while actually ruling on their own account. Among the coalition were also the private troops and former Shuofang soldiers led by the Tang rebel Pugu Huai'en, Military Deputy Commander of the Hebei region; Pugu was the figurehead to whom the whole host was addressed, but the real command remained in the hands of the Tibetan and Uyghur commanders. The Tang was the legitimate party in terms of title, and in practice it was held together by the reputation of the veteran general Guo Ziyi and by the surviving troops, grain stores and fortifications of Guanzhong.
people: 郭子儀是本戰役的實際主持者。廣德元年（763）吐蕃入長安，他以兵部尚書、汾陽郡王之重，總領諸軍收復西京，聲望及於塞外，吐蕃、回紥與僕固懷恩皆畏其名。代宗李豫即位後對邊將猜忌，僕固懷恩兵權被削、召還宿衛，又受樞密使程元振進讒，遂生怨望，764年八月藉外敵來犯之名率叛眾與吐蕃、回紥合兵，兵鋒直指奉天。僕固懷恩出自鐵勒僕固部，一般認為其母為回紥王女，自幼長於蕃中，與回紥有姻親之誼，這是他能引回紥萬眾入犯的緣由。守城的白孝德是安史之亂中在靈州大破史思明的宿將，與郭子儀同出朔方，行軍用兵素為穩重，見敵人兵盛而援軍未至，遂閉城拒守不戰。率援軍赴邠州的郭晞是郭子儀第三子，年少果敢，敢於夜襲；右兵馬使李國臣為其接應。吐蕃與回紥的領兵者姓名散見於同年及次年蕃漢戰役的記載，如達扎路恭、尚野息、尚結息贊磨、尚息東贊等；聯軍雖眾而各懷異心，號令不齊。資治通鑑卷二百二十三所載，是本戰役最完整的記錄。
peopleEn: Guo Ziyi was the man who really ran the campaign. When the Tibetans seized Chang'an in the previous year, 763, it was he, then Minister of War and Prince of Fenyang, who took charge of the armies that recovered the western capital; his fame reached beyond the frontier, and the Tibetans, the Uyghurs and Pugu Huai'en alike were wary of his name. Emperor Daizong, Li Yu, was by nature suspicious of frontier commanders, and after Pugu Huai'en's command had been stripped and he himself recalled to the capital, and after further slander from the Commissioner of the Secretariat, Cheng Yuanzhen, the court's mistrust of the border generals turned the army's heart away from the throne. Pugu Huai'en, who had earned his rank in the suppression of the An Lushan rebellion, nursed his resentment and in the eighth month of 764 called in foreign troops under cover of the renewed Tibetan pressure, aiming his spears straight at Fengtian. Pugu came from the Jieluo tribe of the Pugugu, and his mother was generally held to be a daughter of a Uyghur king, so that he had been raised in the steppe and was bound to the Uyghurs by marriage ties; that kinship was what allowed him to bring a Uyghur host into the war. The garrison commander Bai Xiaode was a veteran who had broken Shi Siming at Lingzhou during the An Lushan rebellion, and came from the same Shuofang tradition as Guo Ziyi; seeing that the enemy was strong and the relief force had not yet arrived, he shut the city and refused to fight. Guo Xi, who led the relief column, was Guo Ziyi's third son, young and resolute and willing to launch a night attack, with Li Guochen covering him. On the Tibetan side the commanders whose names survive belong mainly to the campaigns of the same and the following year, among them figures such as Dadalugong, Shangyeixi, Shangjiexizanmo and Shangxidongzan; the coalition was numerous but each part held its own counsel, and orders did not run cleanly. The clearest account of the whole operation is preserved in the Zizhi Tongjian, juan 223, in the Annals of Tang.
kits: 卡面所繪為亞述長矛，即公元前九世紀兩河流域的短柄長刃冷兵器，鐵鏃或青銅矛頭安於不長木柄，講求以密集長兵抵禦車馬與結陣衝鋒，並與弓、斧相配合。該器物自然不曾出現在唐代的戰場上，但它所代表的功能，在邠州防線上是由唐軍與蕃軍各自的長柄矛承接。唐軍步兵以長槊、長矛為骨幹，配唐刀、匕首與弓箭，鎧甲以札甲為主；朔方、邠寧兩鎮素產良馬，騎兵可用長矛與弓箭作戰，馬上以長刀劈砍；守城則靠弓弩、矢石與城頭的長兵拒止。吐蕃與回紥的兵員以騎兵為主，多用長柄矛與標槊，人馬均披皮甲或小鐵片札甲；回紥騎兵慣於散射、迂迴、衝擊之後立即離開，吐蕃步兵則以長矛結陣護住騎兵側翼。雙方的攻城手段都相當原始，聯軍久攻不克，正是因為缺乏足以對付夯土城垣的攻城塔與撞槌。軍需方面，吐蕃自河隴運糧多靠牛馬馱載，回紥自漠北遠來則以馬肉乳酪為主食，唐軍關中存糧有限，卻有涇渭一線的倉廩，也有西征以來繳獲的馬匹可用。戰後論者常把兩軍所用的冷兵器並列，說唐代的長矛不過是亞述式長兵在東土的後裔。
kitsEn: What the card face shows is the Assyrian spear: a short-hafted, long-bladed weapon of the ninth century BC in Mesopotamia, its iron or bronze head fitted to a shaft of no great length, designed for dense ranks of long weapons to hold off chariots and to meet a charge in formation, and used together with the bow and the axe. That object naturally never appeared on a Tang battlefield, but the function it embodies was carried on the Binzhou line by the long-shafted spears of the Tang and of the Tibetans alike. Tang infantry were built on long sha and long spears, supported by Tang sabres, daggers and bows, with lamellar armour; the Shuofang and Binning commands had long been famous for their horses, so the cavalry could fight with spear and bow and strike from the saddle with the long sabre, while the defence of the walls relied on crossbows, arrows and stones, and on the long weapons of the defenders on the wall. The Tibetans and Uyghurs were for the most part cavalry, using long spears and javelins, with men and horses wearing leather or small iron lamellae; Uyghur riders were used to shooting at a distance, wheeling about, and breaking off immediately after the charge, while the Tibetan foot formed up with long spears to shield the flanks of the mounted troops. The siege equipment of both sides was primitive, and the coalition failed to take the city precisely because it lacked siege towers and rams capable of dealing with a rammed-earth wall. On the logistics side the Tibetans brought grain out of Hexi and Long largely on pack oxen and horses, the Uyghurs came far from the northern steppe living mainly on horse meat and dairy, and the Tang had limited grain in Guanzhong but did have the granaries along the Jing and Wei valleys, as well as the horses captured in the western campaigns. Later writers have often set the cold weapons of the two armies side by side, remarking that the Tang long spear was after all a descendant in the East of the Assyrian long weapon.
tactics: 郭子儀的處置貫穿全戰。第一步是避其銳氣：他判斷僕固懷恩引番軍深入唐境，求的是速戰，唐軍若出城浪戰而敗，軍心立刻離散，於是下令諸營閉壁不出，甚至傳令敢言戰者斬，把怯戰的形象做足。次步是示形惑敵：十月初七夜，唐軍出數萬人列陣於乾陵以南，拂曉前廣布旗幟，遠望如十萬大軍；僕固懷恩與吐蕃、回紥聯軍已在乾陵以北列陣二十里，準備趁曉襲唐軍，見唐軍有備，驚而不敢交戰，遂引兵退去。關鍵一擊是郭晞的夜襲：他以步兵五千、騎兵五百自西南方向逼近，白天只與敵相持不戰，待聯軍入夜鬆懈戒備，即以精銳馬步軍三千人銜枚潛進，突入營中，殺傷千餘人，生擒八十三人，奪戰馬五十匹，俘大將四名。十月十三日聯軍再攻邠州東門不下，十四日雙方在南原接戰，唐軍連戰皆勝，聯軍大潰，追殺數十里，到二十一日聯軍涉過涇水北遁，邠州之圍才解。整個過程靠的是堅壁、示弱、夜襲三招，而不是正面硬撼聯軍的騎兵優勢。聯軍自身則犯了兵多而分、圍城而無器械、久屯而糧道拉長的毛病，最後在進退失據中撤退。
tacticsEn: Guo Ziyi's handling of the business runs right through the campaign. The first step was to refuse the enemy's edge: he judged that Pugu Huai'en had led the foreign troops deep into Tang territory precisely because he wanted a quick decision, and that if the Tang army sallied out and was beaten the morale of the troops would dissolve at once, so he ordered the camps to stay behind their walls and even had it proclaimed that anyone who spoke of battle would be beheaded, in order to build up the image of a frightened army. The second step was to show a false shape and dazzle the enemy: on the night of the seventh day of the tenth month the Tang brought out tens of thousands of men and drew them up south of the Qianling tomb, and before dawn spread flags so widely that from a distance the host looked like a hundred thousand men; Pugu Huai'en and the Tibetan-Uyghur coalition had already drawn up in line twenty li north of the tomb, intending to strike the Tang camp at daybreak, and when they saw that the Tang were ready they were startled and dared not give battle, and withdrew. The decisive stroke was Guo Xi's night attack: with five thousand foot and five hundred horse he closed from the south-west, stood off the enemy through the day without engaging, and waited until the coalition relaxed its guard after dark, at which point he led three thousand picked men of horse and foot forward without a sound, broke into the camp, killed and wounded more than a thousand, took eighty-three prisoners, seized fifty war-horses and captured four commanders. On the thirteenth the coalition attacked the east gate of Binzhou and was repulsed; on the fourteenth the two sides met at Nanyuan, the Tang won engagement after engagement, the coalition broke up and was pursued for tens of li, and only on the twenty-first, when the coalition crossed the Jing River and withdrew north, was the siege of Binzhou lifted. The whole business rested on three devices, holding the walls, showing weakness and striking by night, rather than on trying to match the coalition's cavalry in open fight. The coalition itself made the classic mistakes: too many men spread too thin, a siege carried out without siege engines, and a long stay that stretched its supply line, and it finally withdrew without knowing which way to turn.
data: 可考之數字集中在兵員與日期兩端。僕固懷恩所引吐蕃、回紥之眾，總數約十萬，先取奉天，再分兵二萬餘人自靈武方向進攻邠州；九月二十日郭子儀命郭晞率一萬援軍西出，九月二十六日兩軍遇於宜祿，白孝德與郭晞合擊，敗敵一千餘人，生擒蕃將數人。十月初八拂曉，郭晞所部投入進攻的為步兵五千、騎兵五百；當夜真正投入夜襲的精銳馬步軍為三千，戰後計斬殺一千餘人，生擒八十三人，奪取戰馬五十匹，俘大將四名。聯軍陣地北起乾陵，列陣長達二十里；唐軍出戰地點在乾陵以南。時間線上，兵起於廣德二年八月，郭子儀九月奉命出鎮奉天、屯涇陽，九月二十日援軍出發，十月初七夜布陣，初八拂曉相持，十三日攻東門失利，十四日南原大勝，二十一日聯軍渡涇水而去，前後不足三月。參照前一年，廣德元年十月吐蕃軍入長安，據城十三日即行撤退，說明當時蕃軍並無久占長安之意，本戰之役亦不過以邠、奉一線為進退之地。至於各部實際到場人數，史料多不載，或謂十萬為號召之數而非點驗之數，諸說並存，姑存其概。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked are concentrated in the numbers of men and in the calendar. The Tibetans and Uyghurs led by Pugu Huai'en are said to have numbered some hundred thousand in all; they took Fengtian first, and then detached more than twenty thousand men from the direction of Lingwu to attack Binzhou. On the twentieth day of the ninth month Guo Ziyi ordered Guo Xi to take ten thousand men west in relief, and on the twenty-sixth the two sides met at Yilu, where Bai Xiaode and Guo Xi struck together, defeated more than a thousand of the enemy and took a number of Tibetan commanders alive. At the dawn of the eighth day of the tenth month the force Guo Xi committed to the attack was five thousand foot and five hundred horse; the picked horse and foot that actually went in during the night attack numbered three thousand, and the reckoning afterwards was more than a thousand killed, eighty-three prisoners, fifty war-horses taken and four commanders captured. The coalition's line ran from the Qianling tomb northward for a length of twenty li, while the Tang deployed to the south of the tomb. As to the sequence of events: the army was raised in the eighth month of the second year of Guangde; in the ninth month Guo Ziyi was ordered to the front and camped at Jingyang; on the twentieth the relief column set out; on the night of the seventh day of the tenth month the Tang arrayed; at daybreak on the eighth the two armies stood facing each other; on the thirteenth the assault on the east gate failed; on the fourteenth there was a great victory at Nanyuan; and on the twenty-first the coalition crossed the Jing River and went away, the whole affair lasting under three months. For comparison, in the tenth month of the first year of Guangde the Tibetans entered Chang'an and withdrew after holding the city thirteen days, which shows that the invading army had no thought of staying in the capital for long; the present campaign likewise treated the line of Binzhou and Fengtian as no more than a place from which to advance or to withdraw. As for the numbers actually present from each contingent, the sources mostly do not record them; the figure of one hundred thousand may be a number of proclamation rather than of a head count, and since several accounts stand side by side it is best left as a rough figure.
cause: 戰事起於唐廷內部的失和。僕固懷恩原是平定安史之亂的元勳，僕固懷恩出自鐵勒僕固部，其父亦為本部宿將，代宗即位之初以僕固懷恩為河北副元帥，讓鎮河朔，倚為長城。然而代宗素性猜忌，懼其擁兵自重，先是罷其兵權、召還宿衛，又聽信樞密使程元振之讒，連郭子儀也幾遭貶黜，軍心由此離散。僕固懷恩自負宿功，怨望既深，便藉朝廷與吐蕃、回紥交兵之機引外兵內應，圖的不只是報復，更是要藉蕃騎之威脅京師，逼朝廷重新給予兵柄，同時把唐廷西部邊防崩壞與藩鎮跋扈的責任轉嫁到自己身上。外部條件同樣具備：廣德元年吐蕃已一度攻入長安，河隴、涇原多年征伐，兵制解體，邊軍欠餉、將校離心，涇原、朔方諸鎮的戰力遠不如開元、天寶之世；而唐廷府庫空虛，長安殘破，供養大軍與遠征之師都極為吃力。於是內怨與外敵一拍即合，八月的大舉進兵便是必然。
causeEn: The war grew out of a breakdown of trust inside the Tang court. Pugu Huai'en had been one of the great men who had settled the An Lushan rebellion; his father, Pugu Yang, came from the Jieluo tribe of the Pugugu, and the early years of Daizong's reign saw Pugu Huai'en made Military Deputy Commander of the Hebei region and left to hold that territory, in whom the court placed a long wall against the north. But Daizong was suspicious by nature and feared a commander who would hoard troops and grow strong: first his command was stripped and he was summoned back to the capital, then the court listened to the slander of Cheng Yuanzhen, Commissioner of the Secretariat, and even Guo Ziyi came close to being removed. The hearts of the soldiers turned away from the throne. Pugu Huai'en, proud of his old services and nursing a deep grievance, seized the opportunity offered by the renewed fighting between the court and the Tibetans and the Uyghurs to bring foreign troops inside the frontier. His aim was not merely revenge; by using the threat of the western and northern horsemen against the capital he meant to force the court to give him back military command, and at the same time to transfer to himself the blame for the ruin of the western defences and for the arrogance of the regional commands. The external conditions were equally ripe: the Tibetans had already entered Chang'an once in the first year of Guangde; years of campaigning in Long and Jing had broken down the military system; the frontier armies were underpaid and their officers were alienated; the fighting quality of the Jingyuan and Shuofang commands was far below that of the Kaiyuan and Tianbao years; and the treasury was empty and Chang'an was in ruins, making it extremely hard to feed a great army or to maintain a distant expedition. Internal grievance and foreign enemy thus met, and the great advance of the eighth month was the inevitable result.
impact: 邠州保住了，關中也就保住了。此役之後，吐蕃、回紥聯軍退回河隴與漠北，京師長安未再淪陷，唐廷得以在關中重整財政、修復城防，郭子儀的宿將威望更增至無人敢疑的地步；僕固懷恩所挾外勢要挾朝廷的算盤完全落空，連帶他在朔方、河朔的部眾也人心離散。僕固懷恩次年永泰元年（765）病逝於允州，朝廷一度贈以太尉，其所領的蕃漢混合兵力隨之瓦解；其子僕固瑒等後來再圖起兵，於建中之世為朝廷平定，家族勢力至此斷根。從更大的格局看，邠州一役顯示唐廷已無力單獨抵禦河隴的蕃軍，邊防從兵轉向援，向回紥借兵、向吐蕃和談，成為此後數十年的既定方略，781年唐蕃清水之盟及其後的諸次會盟，皆以此為背景。軍鎮方面，朔方、邠寧兩鎮因守城有功而地位更重，節度使與牙兵勢力逐步坐大，埋下中晚唐藩鎮割據的種子。邠州城自此成為西北邊防的樞紐，歷唐數十年而地位不衰，咸通年間吐蕃再犯時節度使郭曜據城拒守，又是一段與本役相呼應的史事。
impactEn: Binzhou was saved, and with it Guanzhong. After the campaign the Tibetan-Uyghur coalition withdrew to the Long region and the northern steppe, Chang'an was never taken again, and the court was able to put its finances in order in Guanzhong and repair its defences; the reputation of the veteran Guo Ziyi rose to a point where no one dared question it, while the plan of Pugu Huai'en to use foreign power to browbeat the court failed completely, and the men he held in Shuofang and Hebei lost heart along with it. Pugu Huai'en died of illness at Yunzhou in the first year of Yongtai, 765, and the court honoured him posthumously as Grand Commander; the mixed Tibetan and Chinese forces he gathered fell apart with him. His son Pugu Yang and others later rose once more and were put down by the court during the Jianzong era, and the family power was broken at last. On a larger scale the battle showed that the Tang could no longer hold off the armies of the Long region alone; frontier defence turned from soldiers to subsidies and allies, borrowing Uyghur troops and negotiating with Tibet, and that became the standing policy of the decades that followed, with the Qingshui covenant of 781 and the later agreements between the two states all resting on this foundation. As for the commands, Shuofang and Binning gained in standing from their part in the defence, the military governors and their private soldiery grew steadily more powerful, and the seeds of the mid and late Tang military governors' separatism were planted here. Binzhou became a hinge of the north-western frontier, and its position did not decay for the decades that followed; when the Tibetans came again in the Xiantong years, the military governor Guo Yao held the city in resistance, an episode that echoes the one recounted here.
result: 結果是唐軍守住邠州，聯軍失敗而退。十月十三日聯軍攻東門不下，十四日在南原被唐軍擊潰，十月二十一日涉過涇水北去，圍解；唐軍沒有全殲敵人，卻以弱勝強，完成了守土之責。吐蕃與回紥聯軍在關中城下折損千餘人、被俘八十三人、失去戰馬五十匹、四名大將被擒，士氣與補給都受到重創，被迫退回原路；僕固懷恩所期望藉番軍之力重掌兵權的願望隨之破滅，次年即死於軍中。從戰術層面看，本役最值得記取處有三：一是郭子儀堅守不戰、拒絕任何出戰之請，把聯軍求速戰的意願扭成持久消耗；二是以廣布旗幟、虛張十萬的辦法，把唐軍實力不明的信息牢牢握在手中；三是郭晞以三千精銳夜襲敵營，用一次夜間突擊換回整個戰局的轉折，顯示西北邊軍在缺乏大戰經驗、兵器與後勤都不利的情況下，仍可以靠紀律與時機取得戰果。這場戰爭沒有改變唐蕃、回紥之間的基本力量對比，卻明確標誌了唐廷在安史之亂後由盛轉衰的斷點所在。
resultEn: The result was that the Tang held Binzhou and the coalition went away defeated. On the thirteenth the coalition's assault on the east gate failed; on the fourteenth it was broken by the Tang at Nanyuan; on the twenty-first it crossed the Jing River and withdrew north, and the siege was lifted. The Tang did not destroy the enemy, but the weaker side had won, and the duty of holding the ground was discharged. The Tibetan and Uyghur coalition lost more than a thousand men before the walled city of Guanzhong, had eighty-three taken prisoner, lost fifty war-horses and gave up four commanders, and its morale and supplies were both badly damaged, so that it was driven back the way it had come; and with it went the hope Pugu Huai'en had built on foreign arms to recover his military power, for he was dead within the year. In tactical terms three lessons of the campaign deserve to be kept. First, Guo Ziyi fought no battle, refused every request to engage, and turned the coalition's demand for a quick decision into a long attritional contest. Second, by spreading flags widely and pretending to a hundred thousand men, he kept the one piece of information that mattered, the true strength of the Tang army, firmly in his own hands. Third, Guo Xi attacked the enemy camp at night with three thousand picked men, and one nocturnal stroke bought back the turning of the whole situation, showing that the north-western frontier armies, short of great battle experience and handicapped in both weapons and supply, could still win through discipline and the choice of the moment. The war did not alter the fundamental balance of strength between the Tang, the Tibetans and the Uyghurs, but it marks plainly the point at which the Tang court turned from strength to decline after the An Lushan rebellion.
